chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام.
That his father used to consider it recommended that a covering be placed between the deceased and the sky, meaning when he is being given ghusl (ritual bath).

key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the sky, mentioned as part of the recommended covering arrangement
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person being prepared after death
key_terms.سِتْرٌ: a covering or screen placed for concealment and dignity
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: was given ghusl (ritual bath), referring to the washing of the deceased
key_terms.يَسْتَحِبُّ: indicates that the act is recommended, not obligatory

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended to cover the deceased from the sky during ghusl (ritual washing)?
ai.summary: This hadith states a recommended etiquette concerning the ghusl of the deceased: that a covering should be placed between the dead person and the sky during washing. It reflects the preservation of dignity and modesty for the deceased in funerary rites.
